subject: Claude CCAF: Claude Code Configuration & Workflows
description: Slash commands in .claude/commands/, $ARGUMENTS substitution, SKILL.md, context: fork, and plugin packaging.

questions.question: A custom Agent Skill with context: fork generates verbose output while the main session context stays clean. When should context: fork be used?
options: Forking creates overhead and should be avoided unless absolutely necessary.
context: fork is required for all custom skills to maintain context cleanliness.
Use context: fork when a skill generates verbose output that would pollute the main context.
context: fork only for skills invoking external tools or MCP servers.
questions.answer: Use context: fork when a skill generates verbose output that would pollute the main context.
questions.source: UD3-006 | Claude Code skills · Effective context engineering
questions.explanation: context: fork runs the skill in an isolated sub-agent context so thousands of lines of intermediate logs/search results do not pollute the parent session window.
questions.examTrick: Verbose skill output = context: fork in SKILL.md frontmatter.

questions.question: Invoking /migrate users_table — which substitution variables inside SKILL.md can access the argument?
options: process.argv[2] contains it, passed through to the shell.
${input} contains it and arguments must be parsed manually.
$ARGUMENTS contains users_table and $1 contains it as the first positional argument.
questions.answer: $ARGUMENTS contains users_table and $1 contains it as the first positional argument.
questions.source: UD3-056 | Claude Code slash commands — arguments · Claude Code skills
questions.explanation: Slash commands and skills expose $ARGUMENTS (the complete argument string) and positional variables ($1, $2, etc.).
questions.examTrick: Slash command argument variables: $ARGUMENTS (full string) and $1, $2 (positional).

questions.question: Which element of a Skill definition determines whether Claude invokes it for a given request?
options: The list of allowed_tools in the manifest.
The Skill's load order in the skills directory.
questions.explanation: The skill's description field in YAML frontmatter is the semantic matching trigger Claude evaluates against the user prompt.
questions.examTrick: Skill invocation matching is determined solely by the description frontmatter field.

questions.question: Does invoking a slash command count as a "turn" in the session?
options: No — they bypass per-turn limits as pre-approved built-in shortcuts.
No — they run on a separate channel and do not consume context.
They count as half a turn for context budgeting.
Yes — the resolved prompt is sent to Claude as a normal user turn and counts toward context and any per-turn limits.
questions.answer: Yes — the resolved prompt is sent to Claude as a normal user turn and counts toward context and any per-turn limits.
questions.source: BU3-006 (§3.2) | Claude Code slash commands · Context windows
questions.explanation: Slash commands are expanded client-side into prompt text and sent as standard user turns, consuming tokens and turn counts identically to manual prompts.
questions.examTrick: Slash commands expand into standard user turns and count toward context tokens and turn limits.
